description: TEAM IAMNATTY is a passionate group of engineering students driven by curiosity, creativity, and innovation. We are interested in space exploration, Earth sciences, AI, software development, and data analysis. Through the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, we aim to transform scientific data into meaningful insights and develop innovative solutions to real-world Earth system challenges. We believe in teamwork, continuous learning, and turning ideas into impact.

### TerraPulse AI – The Earth Change Intelligence Engine

TerraPulse AI is an environmental intelligence platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It uses NASA POWER satellite-derived environmental data to explore and understand changes in Earth's environmental systems across different geographical locations.

The platform analyzes key environmental parameters, including temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, and solar radiation. Using statistical techniques such as the Mann–Kendall trend test and Sen's slope estimation, it identifies long-term environmental trends, detects unusual observations, and compares regions experiencing opposite environmental changes.

TerraPulse AI features an interactive global research map, environmental trend analysis, anomaly detection, regional comparisons, an AI-powered research assistant, and automated research reports.

By transforming complex environmental datasets into accessible visualizations and statistical insights, TerraPulse AI helps users investigate where environmental conditions are changing, how they are changing, and which regions exhibit contrasting patterns. Its goal is to make Earth system data easier to explore, interpret, and understand.
details:
TerraPulse AI – The Earth Change Intelligence Engine

TerraPulse AI is an interactive environmental analysis platform designed to help users understand how Earth's climate and environmental conditions change over time. It addresses the challenge of identifying long-term environmental trends, detecting unusual changes, and comparing how different regions of the world respond to changing environmental conditions.

What does the project do and how does it work?

TerraPulse AI uses daily gridded environmental data from NASA POWER to analyze four important environmental variables: temperature (T2M), precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), relative humidity (RH2M), and solar radiation (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN).

Users can select locations through an interactive global map or enter research coordinates. The platform retrieves the relevant environmental data and presents it through interactive time-series charts, monthly and annual summaries, and seasonal analysis.

It also applies scientific statistical methods, including the Mann–Kendall trend test and Sen's slope estimator, to identify increasing or decreasing trends. Its anomaly detection system uses robust Z-scores and the Interquartile Range (IQR) method to identify unusual environmental observations.

Another feature is the Opposite-Trend Comparison, which allows users to compare two geographical locations and identify situations where the same environmental variable follows different trends. A rule-based AI Research Assistant helps users interpret the analyzed data, while the research report feature allows users to generate and export findings.

What benefits does it have?

  • Makes NASA environmental data easier to explore and understand.
  • Helps identify long-term climate and environmental trends.
  • Detects unusual environmental observations that may deserve further investigation.
  • Enables comparisons between different geographical regions.
  • Provides interactive visualizations and statistical analysis in one platform.
  • Helps students, researchers, and environmental enthusiasts explore data-driven environmental questions.
  • Supports research documentation through downloadable CSV data and printable reports.

What is the intended impact?

The main goal of TerraPulse AI is to make environmental data analysis more accessible, interactive, and understandable. By transforming large datasets into meaningful visualizations and statistical findings, the platform encourages users to investigate environmental changes across different regions.

It can support educational activities, preliminary environmental research, and greater awareness of how environmental variables change over time. Ultimately, we want to encourage people to become Earth System Trend Detectives by exploring real data rather than relying only on assumptions.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software were used?

TerraPulse AI was developed as a full-stack web application using:

Frontend

  • React with TypeScript
  • Vite
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Recharts for interactive data visualization
  • MapLibre for interactive geographical mapping

Backend

  • Python
  • FastAPI for API development
  • Pandas and NumPy for data processing
  • SciPy and Statsmodels for scientific analysis
  • PyMannKendall for trend analysis

Data Sources and Services

  • NASA POWER API for environmental data
  • OpenStreetMap for map tiles
  • Nominatim for geographical location search

Development Tools

  • Visual Studio Code
  • Git and GitHub
  • Node.js and Python

The project is software-based and does not require dedicated hardware or physical sensors.

How is the project creative?

The creativity of TerraPulse AI lies in bringing multiple environmental research capabilities together in a single interactive platform. Instead of simply displaying environmental data, it combines geographical exploration, statistical trend analysis, anomaly detection, opposite-trend comparisons, and an AI-assisted research interface.

One of its distinctive features is the ability to compare locations where environmental variables may be changing in opposite directions. This helps users explore how environmental trends can differ across geographical regions.

The platform also focuses on making scientific analysis understandable through interactive charts, summaries, and automatically generated research reports.

What factors did the team consider?

During development, we considered:

  • Scientific reliability: Using established statistical methods for trend and anomaly analysis.
  • Data accessibility: Using NASA POWER as an accessible source of environmental information.
  • Usability: Designing an interface that can be explored by students, researchers, and general users.
  • Geographical coverage: Allowing users to investigate different locations around the world.
  • Performance: Processing and presenting environmental datasets efficiently.
  • Transparency: Explaining findings based on the available dataset rather than presenting assumptions as facts.
  • Scientific limitations: Recognizing that NASA POWER provides gridded estimates rather than exact ground-station measurements, and that statistical trends alone cannot establish causation.

TerraPulse AI is designed as an accessible research and exploration tool that connects NASA Earth science data with practical, interactive environmental analysis.
